item.claim: Nausea was the most common adverse event with drug R, reported by 12.0% of patients versus 4.0% on placebo.
item.label: supported

result.reason: Nausea is the highest reported TEAE at 12.0% vs 4.0% placebo, matching the claim exactly.

item.claim: Nearly 40% of drug R patients reached HbA1c below 7.0% at week 26, versus about 22% on placebo.
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table shows 39.9% of Drug R patients and 21.8% of placebo patients achieved HbA1c <7.0% at week 26, matching the claim's approximate figures.

item.claim: Body weight decreased by 2.1 kg with drug R and 0.6 kg with placebo at week 26.
item.label: supported

result.quote: Body weight, kg, LS mean change (SE) | -2.1 (0.3) | -0.6 (0.3)
result.reason: The table reports LS mean change of -2.1 kg for Drug R and -0.6 kg for placebo at week 26, matching the claim.

item.claim: At week 26, drug R reduced HbA1c by 0.94% compared with 0.28% on placebo (difference -0.66%, p < 0.001).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports exactly the claimed values for Week 26: -0.94 vs -0.28, difference -0.66, p<0.001.

item.claim: Serious adverse events occurred at similar rates in the two groups (7.0% and 6.4%).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports serious TEAE rates of 7.0% and 6.4% for the two groups, matching the claim.

item.claim: More patients discontinued because of adverse events on drug R (6.0%) than on placebo (2.3%).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table directly shows discontinuation rates of 6.0% for Drug R and 2.3% for placebo, matching the claim.

item.claim: Drug R reduced HbA1c significantly more than placebo at every visit through week 52.
item.label: supported

result.reason: All three reported visits (weeks 12, 26, 52) show significantly greater HbA1c reduction with Drug R vs placebo (p<0.001), consistent with the claim.

item.claim: Hypoglycaemia (glucose below 54 mg/dL) was reported in 4.0% of patients on drug R and 1.0% on placebo.
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports 4.0% for Drug R and 1.0% for placebo, matching the claim exactly.

item.claim: Baseline characteristics were balanced between groups; mean age was 61.2 and 60.8 years and mean HbA1c 8.3% and 8.2%.
item.label: supported

result.reason: The source table reports the exact mean age and HbA1c values for both groups, and no statistical differences are noted, consistent with the claim of balance.

item.claim: Systolic blood pressure fell numerically more with drug R, but the difference from placebo was not statistically significant (p = 0.247).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table shows a larger numerical decrease in systolic BP with Drug R (-3.2) than placebo (-1.9), with a non-significant p-value of 0.247, matching the claim exactly.

item.claim: The HbA1c reduction appeared smaller in patients with eGFR below 60 (difference -0.38%) than in those with eGFR of 60 or above (-0.72%).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table shows difference of -0.72 for eGFR>=60 and -0.38 for eGFR<60, matching the claim's numbers and direction.

item.claim: The treatment effect on HbA1c was consistent across age subgroups (interaction p = 0.61).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports an interaction p-value of 0.61 for the age subgroup, matching the claim of consistent treatment effect across age subgroups.

item.claim: Shifts in ALT to more than three times the upper limit of normal were rare (0.7% on drug R, 0.3% on placebo).
item.label: supported

result.reason: The table reports ALT shifts to >3x ULN as 0.7% on Drug R and 0.3% on placebo, matching the claim exactly.

item.claim: Fasting plasma glucose fell by 24.3 mg/dL on drug R versus 8.9 mg/dL on placebo at week 26.
item.label: supported

result.quote: Fasting plasma glucose, mg/dL, LS mean change (SE) | -24.3 (2.1) | -8.9 (2.1)
result.reason: The table reports FPG LS mean change of -24.3 mg/dL for Drug R and -8.9 mg/dL for placebo at week 26, matching the claim exactly.

item.claim: One patient on drug R and two on placebo died during the study.
item.label: supported

result.reason: Table shows 1 death in Drug R group and 2 deaths in placebo group, matching claim.

item.claim: Drug R did not increase the risk of hypoglycaemia.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The table shows hypoglycaemia occurred at a higher rate with Drug R (4.0%) than placebo (1.0%), contradicting the claim of no increased risk.

item.claim: Gastrointestinal events were mild and transient.
item.label: not_supported
item.note: severity and duration aren't in the table

result.reason: The table only lists TEAE incidence rates by preferred term and does not report severity or duration information, so it does not establish that GI events were mild and transient.

item.claim: Drug R is safe in patients with renal impairment.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The table reports overall safety population TEAE rates with no breakdown by renal impairment subgroup, so it cannot support a claim specific to renal-impaired patients, and it actually shows higher drug-related and discontinuation rates for Drug R.

item.claim: Drug R was well tolerated, with an adverse event profile similar to placebo.
item.label: not_supported
item.note: drug-related 24.0 vs 13.8, discontinuation 6.0 vs 2.3, grade>=3 9.0 vs 6.0

result.quote:
Drug-related TEAE | 72 (24.0) | 41 (13.8)
TEAE leading to discontinuation | 18 (6.0) | 7 (2.3)
result.reason: The table shows notably higher rates of drug-related TEAEs, discontinuations, and Grade 3+ events for Drug R versus placebo, contradicting the claim of a similar adverse event profile.

item.claim: The HbA1c benefit of drug R was consistent across renal function subgroups.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The interaction p-value of 0.04 for eGFR subgroups indicates a statistically significant difference in treatment effect by renal function, contradicting the claim of consistency across renal function subgroups.

item.claim: In patients with eGFR below 60, drug R significantly reduced HbA1c versus placebo (difference -0.38%).
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The 95% CI for the difference (-0.77, 0.01) crosses zero, indicating the reduction was not statistically significant, contradicting the claim of a significant reduction.

item.claim: In the safety population, HbA1c fell by 0.94% at week 26.
item.label: not_supported

result.quote: Change from baseline in HbA1c (%) by visit (full analysis set, MMRM)
result.reason: The table reports results for the full analysis set, not the safety population, so the population claimed does not match the source.

item.claim: Older patients (65 years and above) derived a significantly smaller benefit than younger patients.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The interaction p-value for age subgroup is 0.61, indicating no significant difference in treatment effect between age groups, contradicting the claim of a significantly smaller benefit in older patients.

item.claim: At week 52, drug R reduced body weight by 2.1 kg.
item.label: not_supported

result.quote: CSR-DRX201, Table 14.2.2: Secondary endpoints at week 26 (full analysis set)
result.reason: The table reports week 26 data, not week 52, though the -2.1 kg figure matches.

item.claim: The HbA1c reduction with drug R increased steadily through week 52.
item.label: not_supported

result.quote: Week 26, LS mean change (SE) | -0.94 ... Week 52, LS mean change (SE) | -0.81
result.reason: The reduction increased from week 12 to week 26 but then diminished (from -0.94 to -0.81) by week 52, so it did not increase steadily through week 52.

item.claim: Drug R also lowered systolic blood pressure compared with placebo.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The difference in systolic BP change vs placebo was not statistically significant (p=0.247), so the claim that Drug R lowered SBP compared with placebo is not supported.

item.claim: No safety signals were identified for hepatic or renal function.
item.label: not_supported
item.note: eGFR fell 2.9 vs 1.1; 'no signal' is a conclusion the table can't make

result.reason: The table shows a larger decline in renal function (eGFR) and higher ALT shift rates in the drug group compared to placebo, which the source does not characterize as absent of safety signals.

item.claim: The maximal HbA1c reduction was reached by week 12.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The largest HbA1c reduction (-0.94) occurred at week 26, not week 12 (-0.72), contradicting the claim.

item.claim: Weight loss with drug R was driven by its gastrointestinal effects.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The table reports weight loss magnitude but contains no data on gastrointestinal effects or any causal mechanism linking GI effects to weight loss.

item.claim: Any adverse event was reported by 57.0% of drug R patients and 61.0% of placebo patients.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The percentages are swapped: the source shows 61.0% for Drug R and 57.0% for Placebo, not the reverse as claimed.

item.claim: eGFR increased slightly with drug R over 52 weeks.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The source shows eGFR decreased with Drug R (-2.9), not increased as claimed.

item.claim: Drug R tripled the proportion of patients reaching HbA1c below 7.0%.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The proportion reaching HbA1c <7.0% increased from 21.8% to 39.9%, about 1.8-fold, not tripled; the reported OR of 2.41 is not a proportion ratio.

item.claim: Haematocrit decreased with drug R.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The table shows haematocrit increased (+1.9%) with Drug R, not decreased.

item.claim: Headache was more common with drug R than with placebo (3.7% vs 4.4%).
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The source shows headache was less common with Drug R (3.7%) than placebo (4.4%), contradicting the claim that it was more common with Drug R.

item.claim: Drug R provides an additional blood pressure benefit of 1.3 mmHg.
item.label: not_supported

result.reason: The 1.3 mmHg difference is not statistically significant (p=0.247, CI crosses zero), so the source does not support a claim that Drug R 'provides' this benefit.

item.claim: Grade 3 or higher adverse events were 50% more frequent with drug R (9.0% vs 6.0%), all of them drug-related.
item.label: not_supported
item.note: relatedness of grade 3 events not in table

result.reason: The numeric comparison (9.0% vs 6.0%, 50% more frequent) matches, but the table does not indicate that all Grade 3+ events were drug-related; drug-relatedness is reported as a separate, lower category (24.0% vs 13.8%).

item.claim: Drug R caused urinary tract infections in 5.0% of patients.
item.label: not_supported
item.note: 5.0 vs 4.7 on placebo; incidence isn't causation

result.reason: The table reports treatment-emergent adverse event incidence (5.0% for Drug R vs 4.7% for placebo, nearly identical), which does not establish that the drug caused the UTIs, contradicting the causal claim.
